# Clinical Bench

> Clinical Bench is an Australian marketplace that gives companies on-demand access to
> credentialled doctors, nurses and allied health professionals for commercial work
> outside direct patient care.

## What it is
Clinical Bench matches companies building health products with registered Australian
healthcare professionals for commercial engagements. It is not a clinical service, not a
contract research organisation, and does not run clinical trials.

## Who is on the bench
Registered doctors (GP and specialist), registered nurses, nurse practitioners,
physiotherapists, occupational therapists, pharmacists, psychologists, dietitians,
speech pathologists, paramedics, radiographers, medical coders, and practice
managers and administrators. All Australian based and registration-checked.

## What can be commissioned
- Product testing and validation: a professional uses the product and reports what breaks.
- Advisory boards: senior clinical input on direction, safety and positioning.
- Medical AI evaluation: clinician-in-the-loop annotation, model evaluation and RLHF.
- Process and procedure input: mapping or explaining care workflows.
- Regulatory, quality and ergonomics review.
- Medical writing and clinical due diligence.

## How it works
1. Scope: the company sends a brief describing the problem.
2. Match: Clinical Bench selects a screened professional with relevant experience.
3. Run: the engagement runs to an agreed written brief, mostly remotely.
4. Deliver: findings are written up so the company can act on them.

Engagements are typically matched in days and quoted at a fixed price per engagement.

## Key facts
- Based in Australia; professionals are Australian based and onshore.
- Input is private and professional. It is never a public endorsement or testimonial.
- Registration is checked before matching.
- Engagements are scoped in writing with a fixed fee agreed before work starts.

## Market context
The global healthcare data annotation market is forecast to grow from USD 167.4 million
(2023) to USD 916.8 million (2030), a CAGR of about 27.5% (Grand View Research). Other
analyst forecasts for the same segment range from 21% to 28%. Credentialled clinician
supply is the binding constraint on that growth.
